title: Integral finite-Tor-amplitude complexes form a triangulated subcategory
statement: For the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with characteristic $p$, fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and a scheme $Y$ on which $\ell$ is invertible; put $A_{E,j}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^j$ for $j\geq1$. Let $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)\subset D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived-complete bounded constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], a triangulated subcategory [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated], and for $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ let $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,j})$ be its derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Let $P$ be the property of $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$: $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, and there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] for every $j\geq1$. Then $P$ is closed under isomorphisms and defines a full triangulated subcategory of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]: $0$ satisfies $P$; $K$ satisfies $P$ if and only if $K[m]$ does, for every $m\in\mathbf Z$; and for every distinguished triangle $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ with $K$ and $M$ satisfying $P$, also $L$ satisfies $P$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.46.4 (Tag 08G2, label lemma-cone-tor-amplitude), part (2), applied to the reductions, which carry distinguished triangles of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ to distinguished triangles of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,j})$ and commute with shifts; the integral category follows the blueprint node def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude (literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-def-sf-operations/def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude.md)

proof.text: For each natural index n use the canonical integralDerivedReduction l E Y D hl n, whose exponent is n+1. The existing integralDerivedReduction_exact supplies its shift comparison and triangulatedness. In particular it preserves zero objects and distinguished triangles. No new change-of-rings construction or coefficient presentation is needed.

source.place: Tag 06YY, label lemma-derived-base-change, applied to the identity of the site and the coefficient projection

proof.text: Let Q(K) mean that all reductions have Tor amplitude in one ordered interval [a,b]. Use the proved amplitude_iso helper from lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated on each reduction isomorphism to show that Q is isomorphism invariant. For zero, use that same module's proved tensor_functor helper: for each test module M, its exact tensor functor F computes every K-flat tensor representative. Since F preserves zero, and cohomology preserves zero, every such tensor of a zero derived object has zero cohomology. Therefore each zero reduction has Tor amplitude [0,0], uniformly in n.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, label definition-tor-amplitude, and the zero complex in the derived-tensor construction

proof.text: If Q(K) has interval [a,b], apply the quantitative shift clause of finite_ctf_isTriangulated at exponent n+1, with its positive-exponent proof Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n). It gives [a-m,b-m] for the shift of the n-th reduction. Transport this along the inverse of the reduction functor's shift comparison. The interval is ordered and independent of n, proving Q(K[m]). Isomorphism invariance and shift by -m give the converse.

source.place: Tag 08G2, label lemma-cone-tor-amplitude, translation, as recorded with its interval in lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle with outside uniform intervals [a,b] and [c,e], take [min(a,c),max(b,e)]. Its endpoints are ordered. The proved amplitude_mono helper from lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated enlarges each outside interval to this common interval at every reduction exponent.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, label definition-tor-amplitude: enlarging the interval

proof.text: Apply the exact reduction functor to the triangle. Apply the quantitative extension clause of finite_ctf_isTriangulated at exponent n+1 to its image and the common outside interval from the previous step. This gives the same Tor interval for the middle reduction at every n. Thus Q is closed under middle vertices of distinguished triangles.

source.place: Tag 08G2, label lemma-cone-tor-amplitude, part (2), for each reduced distinguished triangle

proof.text: Mathlib's triangulated-object-property criterion makes Q triangulated from zero, integer shifts, and middle-vertex closure. The existing boundedConstructibleDerivedCompleteIntegral_isTriangulated gives isomorphism closure and triangulation of P, the recorded bounded-constructible derived-complete property. The property integralCtfProperty is definitionally P intersect Q. Mathlib's intersection instances give both conclusions. This preserves the given finite-field datum, all universes, and every hypothesis of the statement.
